title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a fragment that starts mid-sentence. It belongs to a discussion of how the realizations of (pure) motives over a base field K are compared, especially the Tate object Z(1) / P^1.

1) First paragraph. K carries a complete archimedean valuation, so K ≅ C, and the isomorphism depends on a choice (in effect, of √-1 and an orientation). For such choices the comparison map α_∞ sends u to (1/(2√-1 π))·v.
- v is the canonical generator of H^1(P^1, Ω^1). This is the de Rham / Hodge generator, essentially the trace or residue normalisation.
- u is the canonical generator coming from the topological (Betti) or adelic side, i.e. the class of a point or c_1(O(1)) in integral cohomology.
- In modern terms this is the standard period of the Lefschetz motive. Comparing Betti and de Rham realizations of Z(-1) = H^2(P^1) introduces the factor (2πi)^{±1}. Grothendieck notes that the choices depend on the topology of K, i.e. on its structure as a complete archimedean valued field. The 'primitive elements' of H(P^1, Ω) seem to refer to the generators so obtained (the reading of this line is uncertain).

2) Second paragraph. Now K ≅ R; Grothendieck remarks that the isomorphism is unique, since Aut(R) is trivial. One defines as before a function (really a fibre functor) ξ = ξ_K. The definition uses the choice of C as algebraic closure of R. ξ takes values in Z-modules, but now with an action of Z/2Z = Gal(R̄/R).
- To a motive M it attaches ξ(M), a Z-lattice ('ξ-réseau').
- This lattice sits inside the product of realizations ∏_ℓ M_ℓ × M_{∞,C}, where M_{∞,C} is the complex realization obtained by extension R → C.
- The lattice is required to be stable under the Z/2Z action, i.e. the infinite Frobenius F_∞ (complex conjugation acting on the Betti realization of a variety over R).

Purpose: to define the integral Betti structure and the system of realizations for motives over archimedean fields, and the normalisation of the Tate twist. This is part of the 'réalisations' formalism underlying motivic Galois groups and periods.

The neighbouring pages are unrelated Bourbaki typescript (on the reverse) on root systems.
errors: The normalisation 1/(2√-1 π) versus 2√-1 π (and its sign) depends on conventions: orientation, direction of the comparison map, and whether H^2 or H_2 is used. It cannot be checked without the preceding page. No evident mathematical error is visible.

ideas.what: Comparison of Betti/ℓ-adic and de Rham (Hodge) generators for P^1: α_∞(u) = (2πi)^{-1} v with v the canonical generator of H^1(P^1, Ω^1)
ideas.modern_name: Period of the Tate/Lefschetz motive; 2πi normalisation of Z(1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Grothendieck, Deligne); written conventions in Deligne 'Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales' (1979) and Deligne–Milne–Ogus–Shih (1982)
ideas.where_published: The 2πi factor for c_1 appears in Grothendieck's 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) context; also in SGA 4½ / Deligne

ideas.what: For K ≅ R: Betti fibre functor with values in Z-modules with Gal(C/R) = Z/2 action, and integral lattices in ∏_ℓ M_ℓ × M_{∞,C} stable under Z/2
ideas.modern_name: Betti realization with infinite Frobenius F_∞; integral (Z-) structure on the system of realizations (adelic lattice compatible with the comparison isomorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1979, realizations with F_∞); Jannsen (mixed realizations, 1990); Grothendieck's motive program as relayed by Saavedra Rivano (1972)

ideas.what: Remark that the choices depend on the topology of K (structure as a complete archimedean field), and that an isomorphism K ≅ R is unique
ideas.modern_name: Dependence of Betti realization on the archimedean place / embedding

missed.claim: This is an early (c.1969–72) handwritten formulation of the Betti realization over R as Z-modules with Z/2 = Gal(C/R) action, together with an integral lattice inside ∏_ℓ M_ℓ × M_{∞,C}. It predates Deligne's 1979 F_∞ formalism, but contains nothing beyond what became standard.
missed.quote: à valeurs dans les modules sur Z ... mais avec action de Z/2Z = Gal(R̄/R) ... stables par le groupe Z/2Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historically: it documents that Grothendieck's own motive notes already treated integral and real structures on realizations, and not just Q-structures.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine normalisations (the 2πi period of P^1, the F_∞ action over R, integral lattices across realizations) that became standard through Deligne and others. The interest is purely historical and early-dated.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 probably begins 'éléments de K' — it is the continuation of a sentence from the missing previous page of these notes (the previous page in the scan is unrelated Bourbaki material).
'H(P^1, Ω)' at the end of the first paragraph is likely H^1(P^1, Ω^1), written hastily.
'le choix de ℓ comme' is more plausibly 'un choix de C comme clôture algébrique de R'.
'[l'isomorphisme étant d'ailleurs unique]': 'unique' is underlined (emphasis), not struck out.
The insertion reads 'mais avec action de Z/2Z = Gal(R̄/R)', attached to 'modules sur Z'.
The marginal note under ∏ M_ℓ × M_{∞,C} seems to read 'via : R → C' (extension of scalars), not 'variété'.
